beats.say: Mobile ID and e-signature are your digital signature. A document signed with your PIN counts as signed by you.
Scammers call saying "your certificate is expiring" and ask for your PIN or SMS code.
Your PIN and SMS codes are never told to anyone: not support, not colleagues, not your manager.
If your certificate needs renewing, you do it yourself on the official website or at a service centre.

scenes.title: Certificate call
scenes.intro: Someone calls claiming to be signature service support. Read what they say and choose your answer.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answering is not dangerous. What matters is what you say.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: That works too. If you are worried, call the service's official number yourself.

steps.say: Hello, this is MöhürID support. Your mobile signature certificate, excuse me, expires today and will be blocked unless you renew it.
steps.spoken: Hello, <breath> this is MöhürID support. Your mobile signature certificate <cough> excuse me, expires today and will be blocked unless you renew it.

actions.label: How do I renew it?
actions.feedback: The caller starts steering the process. Check the certificate date yourself on the official website.

actions.label: I will call the official number myself
actions.feedback: Right. Find the service's number on its official website yourself.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Good decision. You can end a call that rushes you.

steps.say: You will get an SMS for the renewal. Read me the code and I will enter it in the system for you.
steps.spoken: You will get an SMS for the renewal. <breath> Read me the code and I will enter it in the system for you.

actions.label: I read out the code
actions.feedback: With this code they sign in as you. A code is for your screen only.

actions.label: I do not share codes with anyone
actions.feedback: Right. Real support never asks for a code.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Right. Hang up as soon as a code is requested.

steps.say: The code did not work. A request will now appear on your phone, enter your PIN and confirm it.
steps.spoken: The code did not work. <sigh> A request will now appear on your phone, enter your PIN and confirm it.

actions.label: I enter my PIN and confirm
actions.feedback: That was not a renewal, you signed a document they prepared. Call the signature service's official number at once.

actions.label: I reject the request
actions.feedback: Right. Never confirm a request you did not start yourself.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Right. Hang up and reject the request.

steps.label: The call has ended. What now?

actions.label: Call the service's official number
actions.feedback: Right. Official support can tell you the real state of your certificate.

actions.label: Tell the security team
actions.feedback: Well done. Such calls usually reach several colleagues.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The caller will try again. Reporting protects your colleagues.

scenes.prompt: Find the traps in this message.

messages.text: Otherwise your signature will be revoked.

spots.label: Expires today
spots.explain: Urgency leaves no time to check. You can see the certificate date yourself on the official website.

spots.label: Unknown address
spots.explain: This is not the service's official website. Type the official address yourself.

spots.label: PIN request
spots.explain: A PIN is never typed into a website to "renew". It only confirms a sign-in or signature you started.

spots.label: Revocation threat
spots.explain: Scare tactics are a common scam method. If worried, call the official number.

scenes.prompt: Is this message safe or dangerous?

messages.text: Confirmation code: 482913. Do not share this code. If you did not send this request, reject it.

cards.explain: A normal message when you sign in yourself. No link, and it reminds you to keep the code secret.

messages.text: Your certificate is blocked. Restore it here: mohurid-yenile.test

cards.explain: The link does not go to the service's official website. Open the official site yourself to check.

body.text: I am on leave. My PIN is 4471, sign these documents for me.

cards.explain: Signing with someone else's PIN means signing in their name. Authority is delegated the official way.

body.text: To renew, sign in to the signature service's official website yourself or visit a service centre.

cards.explain: No link, PIN or code is requested. You renew yourself through the official route.

body.text: Etibarname_tam_selahiyyet.pdf is waiting for your signature

cards.explain: You did not start this request. Reject it and tell the security team.

question.prompt: A colleague off sick asks you to sign an urgent document with their PIN.

options.label: I sign it, they gave permission
options.feedback: An e-signature is for its owner alone. Signing with their PIN breaks the rules.

options.label: I refuse and ask my manager to delegate authority officially
options.feedback: Right. The institution delegates authority to a stand-in the official way.

options.label: I write the PIN down in case I need it
options.feedback: Keeping someone else's PIN is risky too. A PIN stays with its owner.

scenes.explain: The PIN is the signature itself. You never give it away and never take someone else's.

points: Never tell anyone your PIN or SMS code, support included.
Renew your certificate only on the official website or at a service centre.
Reject and report any signature request you did not start.
